(1 comment)

Would be nice to have a specific example to motivate the need for a generic solution.

For example a specific accelerator model and what this reset means exactly for that device.
Done, updated commit message

Is there a gerrit topic or links to patches implementing support for this interface?

For example dbus-sensor patches which implement this reset for e.g. some nvidia accelerator.

Or do you want to get alignment on the idea first before starting implementation?

Yes, here is a consumer patch implementing this interface for a PCIe switch device:
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/89529
Thank you 👍
No new interfaces should have "InternalFailure".  What is the caller supposed to do about you having an internal failure in your daemon?

My original thinking was that having a distinct error would help debugging — for example, if the daemon hits an unexpected internal state during reset, the caller would know it's a daemon-side issue rather than a device or permission issue. 
But I see your point that the caller can't really act differently on it. I'll remove InternalFailure and rely on journal logs for daemon-side debugging.
What is a caller supposed to do about a "Timeout"?
My intent was to express "the device didn't respond in time, possibly because it's busy" so the caller could retry.
Done
Why is this a property and not an argument?  I see it is read-only... but that implies that a device can only support a single reset type.  That is surprising.

My original thinking was that the responder firmware decides the reset semantics, so the BMC just reports what the device does. The Redfish flow is also: caller POSTs ResetType, and if not specified, falls back to this property's value as the default.

But you have a valid point — readonly single value forces a one-reset-type-per-device assumption, which doesn't match Redfish's AllowableValues (an array). Would it work better if I:
 - Change the property to SupportedResetTypes as array[enum] (readonly, reported by firmware)
 - The first entry is treated as the default when the caller does not specify a type.
  
This way the device can advertise multiple types, and the caller picks one explicitly. WDYT?
Thanks!

> Would it work better if I:

👍
Done
Not sure why we need to associate specifically to these types?  Can it be associated to any Inventory.Item?
Agreed, I'll change it to xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item so any inventory item can be the endpoint.

RequestReset then?

Should this be a PendingReset property instead that you write to?  Then we don't need a custom ResetComplete signal either because the property will already emit a PropertiesChanged signal.

I like this cleaner approach too — thanks for the suggestion. Redesigned with PendingReset property; the daemon clears it to "None" on completion so subscribers can track progress via the standard PropertiesChanged signal.
How would you end up with an InvalidArgument from an enum type?

Thanks for catching this. My original intent was to guard against callers passing a value not in the enum, but you're right — the D-Bus binding layer already rejects those before the handler is called, so InvalidArgument isn't reachable here. 
I'll drop it.
`set`

Agreed, removed the ordering convention. The default reset type when bmcweb receives a request without ResetType is now an implementation-specific decision on the daemon side. 
Or do you think we also need a separate property (e.g. DefaultResetType) to express this explicitly, or is leaving it as a daemon-side detail OK?
Acknowledged
We should not refer to specific applications.
Done
